story_position: Chapter 1 — Beat 14 — The Junction / Hidden Monument
scene_purpose: Pay off the Hollow Watch mural by bringing the party to the ancient crossroads Torren knows as the Junction, reveal that the important monument has been hidden in plain sight beneath vines and moss, expose its stone-and-metal cartographic surface, connect the party's existing Dunmere route and the earlier Southern Briar side access to older Diysean route information, and transition into the overnight cleanup window without adding another combat climax.

sections: Beat 14 — Wayfinder Junction / Six Ways Through
Beat 15 — Wayfinder Camp / Chapter-1 Cleanup Window

scene_context_seed.location_name: The Junction — ancient crossroads south of Briar Passage
scene_context_seed.runtime_note: The Junction is safe after the Briarhide Stalker. Ordinary arrival/exploration shows Cyanis only. At the authored discovery trigger the relevant cast may appear as simple field models while portraits and dialogue box carry most performance. Torren knows the crossroads and route but has never seen the monument. The large central stone is heavily covered by vines and moss and must not read clearly as the mural monument until the party deliberately clears the vegetation. That clearing is an allowed major-story physical interaction, but implementation should use one simple interaction/state swap rather than detailed individual animation. Once exposed, the monument is a broad stone-and-metal cartographic surface, not a tunnel entrance. Preserve current Face terminology: Might, Grace, Perception, Memory, Elements, Ruin. Their map function remains unresolved. The map's southeast alignment corresponds to the already-known Dunmere route. A water/cistern notation corresponds geographically with the earlier overgrown Southern Briar side access, providing the reason to backtrack. One damaged map edge stays unresolved. The party physically copies useful information, but a brief fade/state transition is enough; no long drawing choreography. Torren decides to camp and continue to Dunmere in the morning. No random encounters, boss, Host ambush, collapse, antagonist sting, Prime explanation, bearer explanation, complete route-network explanation, or Entity reveal. Cyanis carries the intact Card and it remains inert.

required_story_beats: Party reaches the Junction Torren already knows as an ancient crossroads.
The important monument from the mural is not immediately recognizable because vines and moss heavily cover the central stone.
The party clears the vegetation in one simple major-story interaction.
The exposed stone-and-metal cartographic surface is revealed; this is Torren's first actual view of it.
The monument is understood as a map/route object rather than a tunnel entrance.
Current Six Face markings appear in the technical/cartographic grammar without their function being explained.
The southeast alignment matches the party's existing route toward Dunmere.
Water/cistern notation corresponds with the earlier overgrown Southern Briar side access and makes that branch worth revisiting.
A damaged map edge remains unresolved.
The party makes a practical physical copy of useful information.
Torren decides the group should camp and continue to Dunmere in the morning.
Junction and Southern Briar remain available during the cleanup window.
